newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 2.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Some lumber traders looked for the door late Tuesday as the market stayed in a dull range during a week of holidays in the U.S. and Canada, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Prices were narrowly mixed. Most wholesalers sold from inventories and distributors filled dealer needs.

The lackluster pace frustrated many producers, who felt that customers needed to buy. Some traders pointed to the rebound in new home sales during May and awaited word on what the Federal Reserve will do with interest rates, Random Lengths said.
Canadian imports as of June 21 were running at 25.8 percent of the annual April/March quota.

Western S-P-F was vulnerable as sales slowed to a trickle by midday Tuesday. More producers quoted Std&Btr 2x4 in the $360s. But some mills took small counters from a $360 asking level. The wides of #2&Btr were stable at mills, but secondaries dipped lower to sell. Some studs sold at $320, others as high as $340.

Eastern S-P-F prices leveled off in slow trade. Holidays in the U.S. and Canada and summer shutdowns at many mills sent traders to the sidelines. Mills fell back on adequate order files, while wholesalers focused on reducing stocks. Dealer inquiries ran heavy to straight-length specs, the agency said.

Southern Pine sales eased from last week's pace but treaters bought enough mixed, quick-shipment loads to push up prices. The #2 2x6 and 2x10 moved best, extending shipping times out two and three weeks. The #3 also moved well, but stud prices lagged.
Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir markets were quiet and prices held of dipped $2-5. Buyers felt little urgency, it said.
Several coast mills left quotes unchanged and listened for counters. Hem-Fir studs were flat, while fir studs rose $2.

Southern Pine plywood sales were spotty and prices on most sheathing and underlayments eroded $2-4. Deeper cuts were reported in the westside zone; buyers said deals well below lists were made with producers who needed to move buildups. Most mills held close to quotes but booked few orders, it said.

Western plywood sheathing and underlayment prices softened as mills lowered prices to sell stock for shipment next week. Sales were muted but producers said some buyers showed more interest for early-to-mid-July shipments. The 1/2-inch 4-ply CDX and 23/32-inch underlayment were the most vulnerable items.

OSB prices were flat to lower. There were spots of activity -- a block was placed in the North Central region Tuesday -- but activity overall was muted. Order files were into the week of July 14 or sooner at most mills. Louisiana-Pacific's mill at Hanceville, Ala., curtailed operations due to a log shortage.
